_comment: Tier-2 for dune::helmholtz#1, #4 and maxwell#2 — one 40x40 grid, k a dune.ufl.Constant so the sweep is free, two compiled modules (P1 and P3). Exact plane wave u = sin(k x) imposed on the whole boundary, so the discrete error IS the phase/amplitude error. Measured 2026-08-06 (dune-fem 2.12.0.2): relative L2 error 1.117784e-01 at 20 elements per wavelength (k=12.57), 6.259823e-01 at 10 (k=25.13), 9.543712e-01 at 4 (k=62.83) — strictly monotone in resolution, and below five elements per wavelength the error is far past 'tens of per cent'. On the SAME mesh at k=62.83, P3 gives 4.604336e-02 against P1's 9.543712e-01, a factor of 21. NUMBERS IN THE CLAIMS THAT DO NOT HOLD, recorded rather than asserted: helmholtz#4's 'ten P1 elements per wavelength for about one per cent' is off by two orders of magnitude here (62.6%), and helmholtz#1's 'P3 recovers phase to < 0.1%' is 4.6%. The DIRECTION both claims describe is what this fixture gates: error falls with resolution per wavelength, and raising the order on a fixed mesh recovers an order of magnitude. That the absolute numbers are so much worse at these wavenumbers is itself the pollution effect helmholtz#1 is about.
